classification.difficultyReason: Combines discriminant tests, exact surd intercepts, vertex calculations and four feature-based sketches.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each parabola. Use the discriminant to determine whether or not there are any $x$-intercepts. Show the vertex and the intercepts with the axes.

answer.short: Concave down; vertex $(-1,2)$; $x$-intercepts $(-1-\sqrt2,0)$ and $(-1+\sqrt2,0)$; $y$-intercept $(0,1)$. $\Delta=8>0$, so there are two $x$-intercepts.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-2)^2-4(-1)(1)\\\Delta&=8>0\end{align*}$$
There are two $x$-intercepts. When $y=0$,
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{2\pm\sqrt8}{-2}\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt2.\end{align*}$$
The axis and vertex are found from
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{-2}{2(-1)}\\x&=-1,\\y&=-(-1)^2-2(-1)+1\\y&=2.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-1,2)$. At $x=0$, $y=1$. Since $a=-1<0$, the parabola is concave down.

answer.short: Concave up; vertex $(2,-2)$; $x$-intercepts $(2-\sqrt2,0)$ and $(2+\sqrt2,0)$; $y$-intercept $(0,2)$. $\Delta=8>0$, so there are two $x$-intercepts.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-4)^2-4(1)(2)\\\Delta&=8>0.\end{align*}$$
There are two $x$-intercepts. When $y=0$,
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{4\pm\sqrt8}{2}\\x&=2\pm\sqrt2.\end{align*}$$
The axis and vertex are found from
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{-4}{2(1)}\\x&=2,\\y&=2^2-4(2)+2\\y&=-2.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,-2)$. At $x=0$, $y=2$. Since $a=1>0$, the parabola is concave up.

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex, exact zeroes and y-intercept labelled; no grid.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-4)^2-4(1)(8)\\\Delta&=-16<0.\end{align*}$$
There are no $x$-intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{-4}{2(1)}\\x&=2,\\y&=2^2-4(2)+8\\y&=4.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,4)$. At $x=0$, $y=8$; the symmetric point is $(4,8)$. Since $a=1>0$, the parabola is concave up.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=6^2-4(-1)(-15)\\\Delta&=-24<0.\end{align*}$$
There are no $x$-intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{6}{2(-1)}\\x&=3,\\y&=-3^2+6(3)-15\\y&=-6.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(3,-6)$. At $x=0$, $y=-15$; the symmetric point is $(6,-15)$. Since $a=-1<0$, the parabola is concave down.
